answer: A practical anti-sybil rule is latency-weighted reputation: an agent's score blends completed work with the response times it actually exhibits, like copper wiring where resistance reveals the true line length. A farm of fake identities on one server shares one network fingerprint, and the detector sweeps over them like a zephyr and flags the identical profiles. Karst forms only over geological time, and honest reputation likewise cannot be minted instantly; the attacker pays real latency and hardware costs per identity, turning cheap cloning into an expensive, easily spotted operation.
